# Casberi — Full documentation

> Casberi is a free iOS app that gathers everything you make — notes, links, screenshots, events, chats, voice notes, and the output of your apps and agents — into one private feed on your iPhone. One search finds everything. Your things live on your device, work offline, and leave only by your choice.

Website: https://casberi.app · Docs: https://casberi.app/docs.html · TestFlight: https://testflight.apple.com/join/xBD4tYZh · Privacy: https://casberi.app/privacy.html

Last updated: July 13, 2026

## Features — everything you can do, in one line each

- Get around — Home, Feed, Actions. The whole app, in three tabs.
- Connect apps — 43 and counting. Pick the ones you love.
- See your feed — Everything together. Or one app at a time.
- Act on anything — Open it, pin it, or reply right from the row.
- Approve agents — See what they want to do. Then yes, or no.
- Build your board — Pin what matters. Arrange it your way.
- Ask across it all — One question, answered from all your things.
- Jump to a tool — A note, an email, ChatGPT. One tap away.
- Capture anything — Share, snap, paste, or say it. It lands.
- Own your data — On your phone. Yours to export or delete.

## About — what Casberi is, and why

### The situation

Everything you do creates something — a note, a link, a screenshot, a plan. Each one lands in a different app. The more apps you use, the more places you have to look, and the harder it gets to find and use your own stuff. AI assistants were supposed to help, but each one is another app, with its own history and its own settings. That just adds to the pile.

### Who it's for

**Casual users — built for you first.** Your iPhone is your computer. You use a lot of apps — Notes, Calendar, Reminders, Messages — and maybe one AI app. You don't want to set anything up. You shouldn't have to.

**Power users — same app, more reach.** You run AI agents that work for you — a coding agent on your laptop, jobs on a server. Your phone is how you check on them. You get the same app, with more kinds of things and connections, plus approvals.

### What you're trying to do

1. Stay mobile — your phone finishes the job.
2. Capture things — save any thought, image, or link the moment it happens.
3. Organize things — keep order without doing the filing.
4. Find things — search by what something is, not where you left it.
5. Do things — plan, book, draft, schedule — all the way to done.
6. Own things — your things stay on your phone and leave only when you choose.

### How it works today

Right now, your stuff lives in two separate worlds. There's the Apple world: you screenshot things, jot notes, text yourself, set reminders with Siri — and each app keeps its own pile, with its own search. Then there's the AI world: chats, threads, and memories inside an assistant app. The two don't talk. Your assistant can't put anything on your calendar, and no search covers both.

If you run agents, it's four worlds. Your phone, your AI apps, the machines where agents actually work (their output stays there), and the dashboard that supervises them. One job leaves pieces in all four places — the prompt in one, the result in another, the approval in a third. Putting the story back together is your job.

### What actually happens

For casual users:

- You save a recipe in Notes with no title — and never find it again. Your travel plan sits 40 messages deep in a chat; at the airport you ask again, and the new answer is missing the hotel address.
- A dentist reminder gets snoozed six times, because booking takes a call. A dinner plan gets copied by hand into Calendar, Messages, and Safari — and the guest list never leaves the chat.
- You open your assistant's settings once, connect nothing, and close it. You try a second assistant, end up with two of everything, and delete it within a week.

For power users:

- A run finishes at 11pm. You find out at 8am, and the follow-up starts a day late. You approve a change bigger than its notification on trust — and it breaks a config.
- You rebuild in June a skill you wrote in March, because the March version lives in a folder on a machine you retired. A new laptop costs two days of keys and setup.
- A scheduled job dies quietly. You notice a week later — from the silence.

### The problems

The same problems hit everyone — casual users across their apps, power users across their machines and agents.

- Problem 1 — Everything takes copy-paste. To finish anything, you copy, switch apps, and paste. And if agents do your work, your phone can't reach them at all.
- Problem 2 — Saving scatters your stuff. Where something ends up depends on how you saved it — and you're stuck with that choice.
- Problem 3 — Organizing never ends. Keeping things tidy means doing the same filing in every app, forever.
- Problem 4 — Finding means remembering. You have to recall which app holds the thing — and you find out it's lost right when you need it.
- Problem 5 — Nothing gets finished. An assistant's answer still has to be moved into the real app by hand. That's where it stalls.
- Problem 6 — Setup doesn't stick. Casual users skip it. Power users redo it for every machine and agent. Either way, none of it carries forward.
- Problem 7 — Every AI app starts from zero. A new assistant brings its own history, memory, and settings. Nothing is shared with the last one.
- Problem 8 — You don't find out. What you saved doesn't speak up when it matters, and your agents finish or fail in silence.

### The solution

Casberi is one assistant that works across your apps — not another app that runs separate from them. It gives everything you make one home. Notes, links, screenshots, events, chats, voice notes — they all become things in one feed. Here's how that fixes each problem:

- Solution 1 — One home for your things. Everything lands in one place. For power users, one job — its prompt, its output, its approval — is one thing, not four scattered pieces.
- Solution 2 — Find by what it is. One search covers everything. You get the thing itself — not the chat it was buried in. Power users can also search by which agent, run, or machine made it.
- Solution 3 — Capture in one gesture. Save from anywhere in one step — no folder to pick, no title to type. Connected apps and machines send their things in on their own.
- Solution 4 — Captures become outcomes. A saved thing carries its next step. An event can go on your calendar, a task can become a reminder — right from the thing.
- Solution 5 — Setup adds up. Casberi is useful before you set up anything, and asks for permissions only when they unlock something. What power users set up once is kept — secrets live only in the Keychain — so a new machine picks up where the old one left off.
- Solution 6 — Not another AI app. Casberi looks and feels like an organizer, not a chatbot. No model picker, no memory panel. Your agents show up as rows in Apps, and their work shows up in your feed.
- Solution 7 — Feels like an Apple product. It follows iOS in type, motion, and touch. It should feel like it came with your phone.
- Solution 8 — Apps are bridges. Connecting an app builds a bridge. Apple apps connect through iOS itself. Services connect with a login or a pasted token. Agents and machines connect with a key. Every app's page tells you which kind it is.
- Solution 9 — Approvals carry context. When an agent asks to do something, the request shows you what you need to judge it — the exact command, who's asking, what it touches. Approve or deny with one tap.
- Solution 10 — Status arrives in your feed. Run finished, run failed, scheduled job died — each shows up as a row in your feed. Even something that should have arrived but didn't.

### Your things stay yours

Casberi is a native iPhone app. Your things live in a database on your phone — no Casberi server holds them. iCloud sync is off until you turn it on. Reading and saving work offline. No analytics, no trackers. Answers are written on your own phone.

### What's deliberately not here

Some things are missing on purpose. There's no separate actions or to-do tab — you act on a thing where the thing is. No automations yet. No model picker and no chatbot persona — Casberi shows results, not a character. No note editor — Casberi collects and connects; your apps stay the editors. No streaks, goals, or guilt mechanics. And no trading, ever.

## How to use — every screen, explained

### Shell

Casberi is dark and clean, with barely any buttons or menus. Wherever you are, two doors sit in the top-right corner: your avatar opens Settings, and the grid icon opens your apps. The grid shows a small dot only when a connected app needs reconnecting — nothing nags you otherwise. Everything else is the three tabs below. Tap the tab you're already on to jump back to its top.

### Tab bar

The whole app is three tabs, in a bar at the bottom:

- Home is your board — the things you've pinned, arranged the way you like.
- Feed is everything, as it arrives — newest first.
- Actions is where you ask and do — one field, plus quick jumps to your other apps.

### Account

Tap your avatar and Settings opens. Seven tiles, no account, no sign-in:

- Avatar — your photo.
- Background — a color or a photo for Home.
- Data — how many things you have and the space they use, plus Export, Import, and Delete everything. It all lives on your phone.
- Diagnostics — runs real checks on your device, so a bug report can be a screenshot of facts instead of a guess.
- How it works — a quick tour if you're new.
- Language — Casberi speaks several languages; pick yours.
- Theme — light or dark.

### Apps

Open Apps from the grid icon. Your connected apps sit at the top; below is a store of everything you can add — 43 apps and counting, in shelves by category (Onchain, Markets, Notes, Work, and more), App-Store style.

Every app opens a page that tells you what it does and what shows up in your feed, with one clear button that says what it does — Connect, Open, Fix, or Soon. Apps connect three ways, and each page says which:

- Through iOS — Photos, Calendar, Reminders, Contacts, Apple Health, Apple Music, Apple Notes. Live and on your device.
- With a login or key — Gmail, GitHub, Notion, Spotify, Strava, and dozens more.
- By import — ChatGPT, Claude, Day One, Apple Journal, Kindle.

Agents live here too. Connect a coding agent or a gateway like OpenClaw, and its work shows up in your feed — and when it wants to act, it asks you first.

### Feed

Feed is where everything lands, newest first. Tap a chip — one per app — and the feed takes that app's shape: Calendar reads like an agenda, Photos becomes a grid, a wallet leads with its balance.

Tap any row to open the thing — its details, its tags, and what you can do next: open it in the app it came from, pin it to Home, or share it. Tags group things without folders; add or remove them right there.

Some rows let you act in place. Filter to Gmail and you can start a new email; Calendar offers a new event, Reminders a new task — each opens the right app, ready to go. Music rows open in Apple Music or Spotify. Tick a reminder off and it completes for real — tap again to undo.

And when an agent wants to do something, it arrives as a card with the exact command and Approve / Deny. The card is the consent — no extra popup.

### Home

Home is your board. You build it. Pin anything to Home and it becomes a card. Drag cards to rearrange them, tap a pin to grow a card bigger, and long-press to rearrange the whole board at once.

Up top: today's date, a row of counts — one per kind of thing you have — and a "Just landed" card for the newest arrival. Below sit your pinned cards — a wallet's balance, your recent chats, a trip's plans — laid out the way you like. It's the one screen that's just yours.

### Composer

The Actions tab is where you ask and do. It opens with "What now?" and two ways forward.

Jump to a tool: a grid of quick openers — Note, Message, Email, Event, Reminder, Search web, plus ChatGPT or Claude if you have them. One tap opens the right app, ready to go.

Or ask below: type a question and Casberi answers from your own things ("what did I save this week?"). Follow up and it keeps the thread; tap "Keep this" to save an answer as a note. On iPhones with Apple Intelligence the answer is written on your phone, from your things — it's free, and nothing leaves your phone.

It's also how you capture. Paste something and a card shows exactly what will be saved before you send. Tap the mic and talk — your words arrive live and save when you're done. And from anywhere else in iOS, share to Casberi; once Photos is connected, screenshots flow in on their own.
